summary.text: A 12-year-old boy presented to clinic with a firm, nodular mass on the medial aspect of the right knee present for about 1 year, with gradual enlargement over the last 3 months and mild tenderness but no pruritus or pain. Examination showed a dark brown-black nodule of about 1 × 1 cm with two small peripheral nodular extensions, without ulceration or crusting, and a negative dimple sign. There was no history of skin or other systemic disease.

Dermoscopy showed blue-red pigmentation areas on a white structureless background and a pinkish red periphery surrounded by brown pigmentation. The lesion was excised with 5-mm clear margins under a preliminary diagnosis of nodular melanoma. Histopathology showed a benign spindle cell tumor with a storiform pattern and hemosiderin deposits, confirmed by Prussian blue staining, without atypia or mitosis.

Immunostains for S-100, SMA and cytokeratin were negative, and the diagnosis of hemosiderotic dermatofibroma was established from these histopathological findings. No recurrence occurred during 1 year of follow-up.
